title: How to run MendKit
summary: A full walk-through of every screen, from first start to reading the results.

sections.heading: Before you start
steps: Plug a laptop into power. Repairs and transfers can take an hour or more.
Save your work and close other programs so their files are not locked.
If Windows is waiting to restart for an update, restart first. Repairs can stall while an update is half installed.
Make sure you have a backup of anything you cannot afford to lose. MendKit takes a restore point before repairs, but a restore point does not protect your personal files.

sections.heading: Starting it
steps: Open MendKit. The Dashboard shows the computer name, system version, processor, memory, free space and drive health.
On Windows, click "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard and answer Yes. Most repair steps are skipped without it.
On macOS and Linux there is nothing to restart. MendKit asks for your password once when a step needs it.
The badge at the bottom left shows whether MendKit has administrator rights, and the version number is underneath.

sections.heading: Simple mode and Technician mode
steps: MendKit opens in Simple mode: Dashboard, Migrate, Updates, How-To Guides and Reports, with plain-language results.
Tick "Technician mode" at the bottom left to add Repair, Tools and Tweaks, the live output panel, exit codes and full logs.
Simple mode only runs the safe recipes and will not continue a repair if a restore point cannot be saved.

sections.heading: Dashboard
steps: Read the cards first. A drive that does not say Healthy should be backed up before anything else.
Click "View all specs and temperatures" for the full hardware list and live temperatures.
Click "Fix my computer" to run Standard service: restore point, drive check, system file repair, disk check, virus scan and cleanup. Allow 30 to 60 minutes.
Under "Other fixes", Health report changes nothing and is a good first run. Network fix resets the network settings and needs a restart afterwards.

sections.heading: What is the problem?
steps: On the Dashboard, pick the button that matches the trouble: slow, no internet, Wi-Fi dropping, pop-ups, updates failing, crashing, printer, sound, Bluetooth or camera.
MendKit runs the checks and fixes for that problem and ends on the results screen. Hover over a button to see how long it usually takes.

"Is this computer worth fixing?" changes nothing. It looks at memory, drive type, age, battery and Windows 11 readiness and gives a keep, upgrade or replace verdict. Run MendKit as administrator for the Windows 11 check.
Under "Other fixes": Network check tests the connection step by step and measures download speed, and Backup checkup tells you whether the computer has a backup.

sections.heading: Preview before anything runs
steps: Choosing a fix opens a preview first. It lists every step in order, what each one does and how long it usually takes.
Nothing changes until you click Start. Back returns without running anything.
A step marked "must succeed to continue" is a safety step, such as saving a restore point. If it fails, the rest does not run.

sections.heading: While a job runs
steps: The bottom panel shows the current step, how long it has run, how long it usually takes, and a progress bar.
You can keep using the computer, but do not start a second job. MendKit runs one job at a time and will tell you if it is busy.
Cancel stops the current step. Steps already finished are not undone.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Green tick: that check passed or the repair worked.
Amber: something to look at, such as available updates or a step that was skipped.
Red: a problem was found that MendKit could not fix. Note the wording and pass it to a technician.
"Skipped, needs administrator" means MendKit was not running as administrator. Restart it as administrator and run the job again.
If the screen says to restart the computer, do it before judging whether the fix worked.

sections.heading: Repair (Technician mode)
steps: Recipes run several commands in order. Single commands run on their own.
Tags show which commands need administrator rights or a restart.
"Continue even if a restore point cannot be created" lets a technician go ahead when System Restore is unavailable. Leave it off unless you have another backup.

sections.heading: Tools (Technician mode)
steps: Tick the tools you want, or use Select all, then "Install selected". Each tool installs through the system package manager.
Status shows what is already installed. Remove uninstalls a tool.
Each tool has its own guide in this section.

sections.heading: Tweaks (Technician mode)
steps: Tick the settings you want on, or click a preset, then click Apply. The results screen shows what changed.
MendKit records the old value of everything it changes. "Undo all MendKit tweaks" puts them back.
Some changes only show after signing out or restarting Explorer.

sections.heading: Migrate
steps: Over the network: on the new computer choose Receive and note the six-digit code. On the old computer choose Send, pick the new computer, type the code and start.
With a drive: choose "Back up to a drive" on the old computer, then "Restore from a drive" on the new one.
Nothing on the new computer is overwritten. A file with the same name but different contents is kept beside it as "name (migrated)".
Saved passwords are not moved. Use "Move saved passwords" for the safe way to do it in each browser.
Afterwards, "Reinstall apps" installs the apps that can be matched on the new computer.

sections.heading: Updates
steps: Check lists what is available without changing anything. Install updates installs them.
On Windows, system and driver updates are installed through Windows Update, which MendKit opens for you.

sections.heading: Reports
steps: Every job is saved. "View results" shows the plain-language summary again.
In Technician mode, "View log" shows the complete output and "Open logs folder" opens the folder to copy logs from.
The top of Reports shows this computer's model and serial number. "Export job history (CSV)" saves the list of jobs for your records.
On any results screen, "Save customer report (PDF)" makes a one-page summary with a health score, what was found and fixed, and a look-ahead.

sections.heading: Undo Center
steps: Lists every setting MendKit changed, with "Put back" beside each, and every tool MendKit installed, with Remove.
Repairs cannot be reversed one by one. On Windows, "Open System Restore" takes the system back to the restore point MendKit saved before the repair.

sections.heading: Get help
steps: "Get help" is on the Dashboard and on any results screen that found a problem.
"Email this report" opens a draft in your mail program with what MendKit found. Nothing is sent until you press Send.
"Open RustDesk" starts remote support. Read the ID and one-time password to your technician. Only do this with someone you contacted yourself.
In Technician mode, save the shop's name, phone and email here so customers see who to contact.

sections.heading: ISO Library
steps: Tick the installer and rescue images you want and click the button to open each official download page.
Copy the downloaded ISO files onto a USB stick prepared with Ventoy. See the Ventoy guide.

sections.heading: Hardware Tests
steps: Open Hardware Tests and pick a test. Starting another test stops the one that was running.
Keyboard: press every key once. Tested keys turn green, and the count shows how many are left.
Screen: the screen fills with one colour at a time. Click to move on, press Esc to stop. Look for dots that stay dark or lit.
Speakers: play the left and right tones separately to prove both channels.
Microphone and Camera: allow access when asked. The level bar should move when you speak, and the camera should show a live picture.
USB ports: plug a device into one port and click Refresh. A device marked new proves that port works. Repeat for each port.
Processor stress test: choose a length and click Start. It records the highest temperatures and saves the result in Reports. Plug a laptop into power first.

sections.heading: Setup Profiles (Technician mode)
steps: A profile is a saved bundle of apps, tools and tweaks for setting up a new computer in one run.
Click Apply to this computer on a profile. MendKit installs the apps and tools, applies the tweaks and shows one result screen.
Click New profile to build your own. Tick the apps installed on this computer copies the app list from the machine in front of you.
Export saves a profile as a file you can carry to another computer, and Import loads it there.
Built-in profiles cannot be changed. Copy and edit makes your own version.

sections.heading: Monthly light maintenance
steps: On the Updates screen, turn on Monthly light maintenance. It runs on the 1st of each month at noon.
The run is silent. MendKit only opens its window and shows a notification when something needs attention.
Tick Also install app updates to have the monthly run update apps as well.
On Windows, turn it on while MendKit runs as administrator so the scheduled run can clean up and scan.
Run it now does the same job straight away.

sections.heading: Leaving a job to run
steps: On Windows, the preview screen has a When it finishes choice: do nothing, restart or shut down.
A restart or shut down waits one minute and shows a Cancel it button.
MendKit shows a desktop notification when a job ends and its window is not in front.

sections.heading: Drivers and firmware
steps: On Windows, the Updates screen offers the computer maker's own update tool when one is in the catalog (Dell, Lenovo, Intel).
Open optional driver updates goes to the Windows Update page that lists maker drivers.
Back up drivers saves a copy of every installed third-party driver before you change anything.
On Linux, the Firmware section uses fwupd to check for and install firmware updates.

sections.heading: Crash Analyzer
steps: Open Crash Analyzer. MendKit reads the last 30 days of crash records: blue screens, sudden shutdowns, hardware and drive errors, and apps that crash or freeze.
The headline names the most likely cause. What was found lists each kind of crash, how often it happened and what it means.
What to do, in order is the repair plan. Each step has a button that opens the right screen or starts the right repair.
On Windows, run MendKit as administrator so it can read the crash dump files as well as the event log.
Technician mode adds the raw detail to each line of the timeline.

sections.heading: Copy from an old drive (Migrate)
steps: Use this when the old computer will not start. Take its drive out and connect it to this computer with a USB adapter or dock.
In Migrate, click Copy from an old drive, then Choose the old drive. Pick the drive itself, its Users or home folder, or one person's folder.
Choose whose files to copy, tick what you want and click Start copying.
Nothing on the old drive is changed, nothing on this computer is overwritten, and saved passwords are not copied.
For a Windows drive, run MendKit as administrator or the old user's folders cannot be read. Unlock a BitLocker or FileVault drive first.
If the drive is failing, copy the most important folders first, one at a time.

sections.heading: Backup image before repair (Technician mode)
steps: Open Backup & Erase. On Windows, connect an NTFS external drive with enough free space, choose it and click Create the backup image. Run MendKit as administrator.
The image is saved in a WindowsImageBackup folder on that drive. Leave the folder where it is.
To put the image back, start Windows recovery (hold Shift while choosing Restart), then Troubleshoot, Advanced options, System Image Recovery.
On macOS this starts a Time Machine backup. On Linux it takes a Timeshift snapshot named MendKit before repair.

sections.heading: Secure erase (Technician mode)
steps: Erasing cannot be undone. Read the name of what you chose twice before you confirm.
Erase chosen files and folders: add them to the list, type ERASE and click Erase them. Each file is overwritten with random data, then deleted. System folders and whole user folders are refused.
Erase free space: overwrites the empty part of a drive so files deleted earlier cannot be recovered. Files still on the drive are not touched.
Erase a whole drive: for an external or second drive. Type ERASE to confirm. The drive this computer runs from is never offered.
To erase the whole computer before selling it, use Windows Reset with Clean data turned on, or boot ShredOS from the ISO Library.
On SSDs and USB sticks an overwrite may not reach every old copy. Erase the whole drive, or use the maker's secure erase tool.

sections.heading: Technician USB and portable MendKit
steps: In Technician mode, open ISO Library. The Build a technician USB card is at the top.
Click Choose the USB stick and pick the stick. Nothing already on it is removed.
Tick Portable MendKit and the ISO files you want. ISO files in your Downloads folder are listed; Add ISO files adds others.
Click Copy to the stick. Copying again later only copies what changed.
On another computer, open the MendKit folder on the stick and start "Start MendKit". Nothing is installed, and logs, settings and undo records stay on the stick in MendKitData.
A portable copy runs on the same kind of system that made it: make it on Windows for Windows computers.
To start computers from the ISO files, install Ventoy on the stick first (see the Ventoy guide). Ventoy erases the stick, so do that before copying.

sections.heading: Working without internet
steps: MendKit checks the connection every minute. "No internet" shows under the Administrator badge when it is down.
Repairs, hardware tests, the crash analyzer, migration, tweaks, backup and erasing all work offline.
Tool installs, updates and ISO downloads need a connection. Fix the network first with "No internet" on the Dashboard.

sections.heading: Reinstall assistant (Technician mode)
steps: Open Repair and click Reinstall assistant. Use it when repairs do not hold.
Read the Before you start list and fix anything marked as a problem. Make a backup first.
Windows 11: Option 1 opens Recovery settings, where "Reinstall now" reinstalls Windows through Windows Update and keeps files, apps and settings.
Windows 10, or when Option 1 fails: download a matching Windows ISO, choose it under Option 2 and click Start the repair install. In Setup, pick "Keep personal files and apps".
If "Keep personal files and apps" is greyed out, the ISO does not match the installed Windows. Stop and get the right edition and language.
macOS and Linux show the steps to follow; MendKit does not start those reinstalls itself.

sections.heading: Weekly backup
steps: Open Migrate. Under Keep a regular backup, click Choose the backup drive and pick an external drive.
Click Turn on the weekly backup. It runs every Friday at 12:30 and copies only new and changed files.
It is silent when all is well. If the drive is not connected, MendKit shows a notice so the backup is not forgotten.
The backup is the same plain folder that "Back up to a drive" makes, so "Restore from a drive" reads it.
The button beside it opens the system's own backup tool (File History, Time Machine) if you want that as well.

sections.heading: Updating MendKit
steps: MendKit checks for a newer version of itself a few seconds after it starts. When there is one, "Update available" shows at the bottom left.
Open Updates. The MendKit itself card at the top shows your version and the new one.
On an installed Windows copy, click Download the update, then Restart and install. If you skip that, the update installs the next time you close MendKit.
A portable or USB copy cannot replace itself. Get the new version opens the download in your browser; run it, or rebuild the technician USB from an updated copy.
An update is never installed while a repair or other job is running.

sections.heading: Offline installers (Windows, Technician mode)
steps: Use this to install tools on a computer that has no internet, or a broken connection you are there to fix.
While online, open Tools, tick the tools you want and click Save selected for offline use. Check download sizes shows roughly how much space they need first.
Saved tools show their version and size in the Offline column. Save them again later to pick up newer versions.

With no internet, Install and Install selected use the saved copies automatically, and the button reads Install from cache. Run MendKit as administrator for this: without the internet there is nothing to ask for permission part-way through.
To carry them to other computers, build a technician USB in the ISO Library and tick Offline installers. The portable MendKit on the stick uses them.
A few tools run without installing; their saved copy is opened straight from the cache folder. Microsoft Store apps cannot be saved.
On Mac and Linux, offline installers are not available yet.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: A step that sits far past its usual time is usually waiting on Windows Update. Cancel, restart the computer and run it again.
If a repair made things worse, open System Restore in Windows and choose the restore point named "MendKit before repair".
Tweaks can be reversed from the Tweaks screen at any time.

title: Remote access audit
summary: Finding and removing remote-control programs, for example after a phone or pop-up scam.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Scammers talk people into installing a remote-control program, then use it to watch the screen or move money. The program often stays installed afterwards.
The audit finds these programs so the owner can see what is able to reach the computer and decide what stays.
The same programs are used honestly by technicians, employers and family. Finding one does not prove a scam.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: On Windows, restart MendKit as administrator first, so it can check every user's folders and remove what you choose.
Open it from the Dashboard ("Check for remote access") or the Repair screen ("Remote access audit").
Click "Scan this computer". It checks installed programs, running programs, services, Program Files, ProgramData and each user's AppData, Downloads, Desktop and Documents. Allow a few minutes.
Read the list. Each program shows where it was found, and whether it is running now or starts with the computer.
Tick the ones nobody recognises or wants, click "Remove selected", read the confirmation and click "Yes, remove them".
If an uninstaller window opens, follow its prompts.
Restart the computer and scan again to confirm they are gone.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "Running now" means the program is active at this moment. "Starts with the computer" means it has a service that comes back after every restart.
"Program file" lines are loose copies, usually in Downloads or on the Desktop, that were run without installing.
Removal closes the program, stops and disables its service, runs its own uninstaller, and moves loose copies to a quarantine folder.
Quarantined files are not deleted. The Undo Center lists them with "Put back".

sections.heading: After a scam
steps: Disconnect the computer from the internet until the programs are removed.
Change the passwords for email and banking from a different device.
Call the bank straight away if any account or card details were entered or shown on screen.
Run "Pop-ups or strange behaviour" from the Dashboard for a malware scan and a list of startup programs.
Anyone who phones again offering a refund or more help is the same scam.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Keep programs your own technician, employer or family set up. Ask before removing one you are unsure about.
Quick Assist is part of Windows and is listed for information only. It connects only when someone opens it and types a code.
The audit recognises a fixed list of well-known products. A program that is not on the list will not be found, so a clean result is not a guarantee.
Removal is built for Windows. On macOS and Linux the audit reports what it finds and leaves removal to you.

title: ClamAV
summary: Open-source virus scanner run from the command line.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: A second-opinion virus scan, or a scan on a system with no other scanner. It finds and reports; it does not watch in the background.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open a terminal (on Windows, a Command Prompt in the ClamAV folder).

Update the virus definitions first: run "freshclam". On Windows the first time, copy the two .conf.sample files in conf_examples into the ClamAV folder, remove the "Example" line from each, then run freshclam.
Scan a folder: "clamscan -r --infected C:\Users" on Windows, or "clamscan -r --infected /home" on Linux. -r scans subfolders and --infected lists only infected files.
For a whole drive, expect several hours. Start with the user folders and Downloads.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Each infected file is printed with the name of the threat and the word FOUND.
The summary at the end gives the count of infected files. Zero means nothing was found.
ClamAV reports more false alarms than commercial scanners. Check a detection by its name before deleting anything.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not use --remove on the first pass. Review what it found, then delete or quarantine deliberately.

title: BleachBit
summary: Frees disk space by deleting caches, temporary files and old logs.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Clearing space on a nearly full drive and removing browser caches and temporary files.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open BleachBit. To clean system areas as well, run it as administrator (Windows) or "BleachBit as Administrator" (Linux).
Tick the categories to clean in the left column. Clicking a category shows what each item does.
Click Preview first. It lists every file and the space that would be freed without deleting anything.
If the preview looks right, click Clean.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The bottom line shows the space recovered and the number of files deleted.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Leave "Passwords" and "Saved form history" unticked unless you mean to erase them.
"Free disk space" overwrites empty space and can take hours. It is not needed for a normal cleanup and should not be used on SSDs.
Unticking cookies keeps the customer signed in to their websites.

title: Bulk Crap Uninstaller
summary: Removes many programs at once and cleans up what they leave behind.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Removing trialware and unwanted programs in one pass, and uninstalling programs whose own uninstaller is broken.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open BCUninstaller and let it finish listing programs.
Tick the programs to remove. The colour key at the bottom marks Microsoft, unverified and orphaned entries.
Click Uninstall for the normal uninstallers, or "Uninstall quietly" to run them without prompts where supported.
Accept the offer to create a restore point.
When the uninstallers finish, BCU offers a leftover scan. Review the list and remove the items marked with high confidence.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Programs disappear from the list as they are removed. Anything that failed stays and can be retried or force-removed.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not remove entries you do not recognise that are published by Microsoft, Intel, AMD, NVIDIA or the computer maker; many are drivers.
In the leftover scan, leave low-confidence items unticked.

title: smartmontools (smartctl)
summary: Reads the health data drives record about themselves.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Checking whether a hard drive or SSD is failing, before repairs or when a computer is slow or losing files.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open a terminal as administrator (or use sudo).
List the drives: "smartctl --scan".
Health verdict: "smartctl -H /dev/sda" (use the name from the scan; NVMe drives look like /dev/nvme0).
Full report: "smartctl -a /dev/sda".
Start a self-test: "smartctl -t short /dev/sda" (about 2 minutes) or "-t long" (hours). Read the result afterwards with "smartctl -a".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: PASSED is the drive's own verdict, but look further: Reallocated_Sector_Ct, Current_Pending_Sector and Offline_Uncorrectable should all be 0 on a hard drive.
On NVMe drives check "Percentage Used", "Available Spare" and "Media and Data Integrity Errors".
Any non-zero pending or uncorrectable sectors, or a FAILED verdict, means back up now and replace the drive.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Some USB enclosures hide SMART data. Try adding "-d sat".

title: CrystalDiskInfo
summary: Shows drive health and temperature in a window.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: A quick, readable drive health check to show a customer.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open CrystalDiskInfo. It reads every drive on start.
Pick a drive with the buttons along the top.
Use Function, then Refresh, to read the values again.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Health Status: Good (blue), Caution (yellow) or Bad (red).
Caution usually means reallocated or pending sectors. Back the drive up and plan to replace it.
For SSDs, the percentage beside the status is the remaining life estimate.
Temperature above about 55 C for a hard drive or 70 C for an SSD is worth investigating.

title: WinDirStat
summary: Maps what is using disk space.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding what filled a drive.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open WinDirStat, choose the drive and click OK. The scan takes a few minutes.
The top left lists folders by size. The top right lists file types. The bottom is a map where each block is a file and its area is its size.
Click a large block to jump to that file in the list. Right-click a file or folder for Explorer Here or Delete.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Sort by size and work down from the top. Common finds are old downloads, video files, phone backups and the Windows.old folder.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not delete inside Windows, Program Files or ProgramData from here. Use Disk Cleanup or the program's own uninstaller for those.
pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys are system files. Hibernation can be turned off from the Tweaks screen if the space is needed.

title: TestDisk and PhotoRec
summary: Recovers lost partitions and deleted files.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: TestDisk repairs a partition table when a drive shows as empty or unformatted. PhotoRec recovers files from a drive, card or stick whose file system is damaged or was formatted.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Never recover onto the drive you are recovering from. Have a second drive ready with enough free space.

PhotoRec: run "photorec" (qphotorec for the window version) as administrator. Choose the drive, then the partition or Whole disk, then the file system type, then the folder on the other drive to save into.
TestDisk: run "testdisk" as administrator. Choose Create for a new log, pick the drive, accept the partition table type it detects, then Analyse and Quick Search.
When TestDisk lists the lost partitions, press P to list files and confirm it is the right one before choosing Write.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: PhotoRec saves files into recup_dir folders with new names, sorted only by type. Expect to sort through them.
In TestDisk, a partition whose files list correctly with P is safe to write back.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: If the drive is clicking, disappearing or very slow, stop. Image it with ddrescue first and recover from the image.
Writing a wrong partition table can make things worse. If unsure, copy the files out with P and C instead of writing.

title: LibreHardwareMonitor
summary: Shows temperatures, fan speeds, voltages and load.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Diagnosing overheating and sudden shutdowns, and giving MendKit full temperature readings.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run LibreHardwareMonitor as administrator so it can read every sensor.
Expand the processor, graphics card and drive entries to see their temperatures.
Leave it open, then use "View all specs and temperatures" on the MendKit Dashboard to see processor and motherboard temperatures there.
Options, then "Run On Windows Startup" and "Start Minimized", keeps it available.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The Value column is the reading now; Max is the highest since it was opened. Run something demanding for ten minutes and read Max.
As a rule, a processor above 95 C or a graphics card above 90 C under load needs cleaning, new thermal paste or better airflow.

title: UniGetUI
summary: Updates and installs apps from winget and other package managers in one window.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Updating everything on a Windows computer in one place.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open UniGetUI and wait for it to load the package lists.
Open the Software Updates tab. Tick the apps to update or use Select all.
Click "Update selected packages". Answer any administrator prompts.
The Installed Packages tab lists what is installed and can uninstall in bulk.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Each update shows as succeeded or failed in the operations list at the bottom. Failed items can be retried.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: An app that is open usually fails to update. Close it and retry.

title: Nmap
summary: Finds devices on a network and the services they offer.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Listing what is connected to a network you look after, finding a printer or camera's address, and checking which services a device exposes.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Find your network range first, for example 192.168.1.0/24.
List devices: "nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24".
Check one device's common ports: "nmap 192.168.1.50". Add "-sV" to identify the services.
On Windows, Zenmap gives the same scans in a window.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "Host is up" lines are the devices that answered, with their address and often the maker.
open means a service is listening on that port, closed means nothing is, filtered means a firewall is blocking the question.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Only scan networks and devices you own or have permission to test.

title: 7-Zip
summary: Opens and creates zip, 7z and other archives.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Opening archives Windows cannot, and packing folders for transfer.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Windows: right-click a file or folder, choose 7-Zip (under "Show more options" on Windows 11), then "Extract Here", "Extract to folder" or "Add to archive".
Command line: "7z x archive.7z" extracts with folders; "7z a backup.7z Folder" creates an archive.
To protect an archive, set a password in "Add to archive" and tick "Encrypt file names".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Errors are listed at the end of the operation. "Data error" or "CRC failed" means the archive is damaged or the password is wrong.

title: RustDesk
summary: Open-source remote desktop for remote support.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Helping someone on their computer from yours, with their agreement.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Install RustDesk on both computers.
The person being helped opens RustDesk and reads out the ID and the one-time password shown on the left.
The helper types that ID under "Control Remote Desktop", clicks Connect and enters the password.
The person being helped can watch everything and end the session by closing the connection window.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: A connected session shows the remote screen. The toolbar at the top has file transfer, chat and display settings.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Only give your ID and password to someone you contacted yourself. A caller who asks you to install a remote tool is running a scam.
Remove RustDesk or turn off unattended access when support is finished.

title: Ventoy
summary: Makes a USB stick that can start a computer from several ISO files.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Building a technician stick with Windows installers, Linux live systems and rescue tools on it.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Ventoy2Disk. Choose the USB stick in the Device list and check the size to be sure it is the right one.
Click Install and confirm twice. This erases the stick.
When it finishes, copy ISO files onto the stick like any other files.
Start the target computer from the stick (often F12, F9 or Esc at power-on) and choose an ISO from the Ventoy menu.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Ventoy2Disk shows the installed version on the stick when it is ready. Update keeps the files on it.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Install erases everything on the chosen drive. Unplug other USB drives first.
Some computers need Secure Boot support enabled in Ventoy (Option menu) or the Ventoy key enrolled on first start.

title: Sysinternals Autoruns
summary: Shows everything that starts with Windows.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding what loads at startup when a computer is slow to start, or shows pop-ups that come back after every restart.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run Autoruns as administrator and wait for "Ready" in the status bar.
In Options, tick "Hide Microsoft Entries" to shorten the list.
Work through the Logon, Scheduled Tasks and Services tabs.
Untick an entry to disable it. Right-click, then Delete, removes it for good.
Right-click an entry and choose "Check VirusTotal" to see whether scanners recognise the file.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Yellow rows point at a file that no longer exists and are safe to delete.
Pink rows have no publisher signature. Many are harmless, but look at each one.
A blank Publisher and Description on a file in a temp or roaming folder deserves a closer look.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Untick first and restart to test. Delete only once you are sure.
Do not disable entries from Microsoft or the graphics, audio and chipset makers unless you know what they do.

title: Sysinternals Process Explorer
summary: A detailed view of running programs.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding what is using the processor, memory or a locked file, and identifying an unknown program.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run Process Explorer as administrator.
Click the CPU or Private Bytes column to sort by processor or memory use.
Hover over a process to see its full path and what it hosts.
Find, then "Find Handle or DLL", shows which program has a file open.
Options, then VirusTotal.com, then "Check VirusTotal.com", adds a scanner score column.
Right-click a process for Kill Process or Suspend.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Purple rows are packed programs, which is common in malware but also in some legitimate software. Pink rows are services, blue are your own programs.
A VirusTotal score above a few detections is worth following up.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not kill System, csrss, wininit, smss or lsass. Windows stops immediately.

title: Malwarebytes
summary: Malware scanner and remover.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: A thorough second scan when a computer shows pop-ups, redirects or other signs of infection.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Malwarebytes and click Scan. The default Threat Scan covers memory, startup items and the usual hiding places.
Let it update first if it offers to.
When the scan ends, review the list, leave everything ticked unless you recognise a false alarm, and click Quarantine.
Restart if asked.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Items labelled PUP or PUM are unwanted programs and changed settings; Malware and Trojan entries are the serious ones.
Quarantined items can be restored from Detection History if something legitimate was caught.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: New installs start a Premium trial with real-time protection. Turn it off in Settings, then Account, if another antivirus is the main one.
The free version is for personal use. A business needs a paid licence.

title: AdwCleaner
summary: Removes adware, browser hijackers and unwanted toolbars.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Browser pop-ups, a changed home page or search engine, and bundled junk programs.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Close all browsers.
Run AdwCleaner (it does not install) and click "Scan Now".
Review the results. Untick anything the customer wants to keep.
Click Quarantine, then let it restart the computer.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The log after the restart lists what was removed. It is saved in C:\AdwCleaner\Logs.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: The "preinstalled software" section lists maker software. Leave it unticked unless you are sure.
Free for personal use; check the licence for business use.

title: HWiNFO
summary: Detailed hardware information and sensor readings.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Identifying exact parts and logging temperatures, voltages and throttling over time.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Start HWiNFO. Tick "Sensors-only" for monitoring or "Summary-only" for a parts list, then click Start.
In the sensors window, each row shows Current, Minimum, Maximum and Average.
Click the logging button at the bottom to record every reading to a CSV file while you run a stress test.
Without the tick boxes, the main window gives a tree of every component with model numbers.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Read the Maximum column after a period of load.
"Thermal Throttling: Yes" on a processor core means it reached its limit and slowed itself down.
Drive entries show remaining life and any SMART warnings.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Free for personal use; a business needs a licence.

title: ncdu
summary: Shows what is using disk space, in the terminal.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding what filled a drive on a system without a desktop, or over a remote session.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Scan a folder: "ncdu /home". For the whole system without crossing into other drives: "sudo ncdu -x /".
Move with the arrow keys. Enter opens a folder and the left arrow goes back.
Press d to delete the selected item, and q to quit.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Folders are listed largest first with a bar showing their share.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: d deletes immediately after one confirmation. Be sure of the path first.

title: GNU ddrescue
summary: Copies a failing drive, working around the damaged areas.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Making an image of a drive that has bad sectors, so recovery can be done from the copy and not the dying drive.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Identify the drives with "lsblk" (Linux) or "diskutil list" (macOS). Be certain which is the failing drive and which is the destination.
First pass, skipping bad areas quickly: "sudo ddrescue -n /dev/sdX /mnt/backup/drive.img /mnt/backup/drive.map".
Second pass, retrying the bad areas: "sudo ddrescue -d -r3 /dev/sdX /mnt/backup/drive.img /mnt/backup/drive.map".
Always give the same map file. It records progress, so an interrupted run carries on where it stopped.
Recover files from the image afterwards with TestDisk or PhotoRec.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "rescued" is how much has been copied and "bad-sector" is how much could not be read.
A finished run with a small bad-sector figure usually gives a usable image.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Swapping the source and destination destroys the data. Read the command twice.
The destination needs at least as much free space as the whole failing drive.
Do not mount or run repairs on the failing drive before imaging it.

title: lm-sensors
summary: Reads temperature, fan and voltage sensors.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Checking temperatures on Linux, and giving MendKit temperature readings there.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run "sudo sensors-detect" once and accept the default answers. It finds the sensor chips.
Run "sensors" to print the readings.
"watch -n 2 sensors" refreshes them every two seconds.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Each reading shows the current value with its high and critical limits in brackets.
Core temperatures near the critical value under load point to dust, dried thermal paste or a failed fan.

title: inxi
summary: Prints a full hardware and system summary.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Getting the exact hardware and driver details in one go, for a job record or a support request.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Full report: "inxi -Fxz". -F is everything, -x adds detail and -z hides serial numbers and addresses.
Just graphics: "inxi -G". Just drives: "inxi -D". Just network: "inxi -N".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Sections are labelled System, Machine, CPU, Graphics, Audio, Network, Drives, Partition and Sensors.
Under Graphics and Network, "driver: N/A" means no driver is loaded for that device.

title: iperf3
summary: Measures network speed between two computers.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Testing the real speed of a cable or Wi-Fi link inside a building, separately from the internet connection.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: On one computer start the server: "iperf3 -s".
On the other, run the test against the first computer's address: "iperf3 -c 192.168.1.20".
Add "-R" to test the other direction and "-t 30" for a 30-second test.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The last lines give the average speed as sender and receiver.
A wired gigabit link should show around 940 Mbits/sec. Much less points to a bad cable, a slow switch port or a 100 Mb device.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: The server computer's firewall must allow port 5201.

title: Timeshift
summary: Takes system snapshots you can roll back to.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: A safety net before updates and repairs. MendKit uses it for the snapshot step when it is set up.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Timeshift and run the setup wizard: choose RSYNC (or BTRFS on a btrfs system), then the drive to keep snapshots on, then a schedule.
Click Create to take a snapshot now.
To roll back, select a snapshot and click Restore. From a system that will not start, run Timeshift from a live USB and restore from there.
Command line: "sudo timeshift --create" and "sudo timeshift --restore".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The list shows each snapshot with its date and tags. The first one takes longest; later ones only store changes.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Timeshift protects the system, not personal files. Home folders are excluded by default.
Keep snapshots on a different drive from the system if you can.

title: GParted
summary: Partition editor.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Resizing, creating and formatting partitions, usually from a live USB.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Start GParted and choose the drive from the list at the top right. Check the size and model.
Right-click a partition for Resize/Move, Format to, Delete or Check.
Changes queue up at the bottom. Nothing happens until you click the green tick to apply.
A mounted partition shows a key icon. Unmount it first, or work from a live USB for the system partition.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The apply window lists each operation with a tick or an error. Save the details if something fails.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Back up first. A power cut during a resize or move can lose the partition.
Double-check the drive selector before applying. It is easy to work on the wrong drive.
Shrink Windows partitions from inside Windows where possible, and turn off BitLocker and Fast Startup beforehand.

title: htop
summary: Shows running programs and resource use in the terminal.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Seeing what is using the processor and memory.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run "htop".
F6 chooses the sort column. F4 filters by name. F5 switches to a tree showing which program started which.
Select a process and press F9 to end it; choose signal 15 first and 9 only if it will not stop.
q quits.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The bars at the top show each processor core, memory and swap.
A full memory bar with swap in heavy use explains a slow computer.

title: topgrade
summary: Updates everything on the system with one command.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Bringing a Mac fully up to date: system updates, Homebrew, and other package managers it finds.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run "topgrade" in Terminal.
Enter your password when a step asks for it.
"topgrade --dry-run" shows what it would do without doing it.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: A summary at the end marks each step OK or FAILED. Failed steps can be run on their own to see the error.

title: Building a technician USB stick
summary: How to turn the ISO Library downloads into one bootable stick.

sections.heading: What you need
steps: A USB stick of 32 GB or more. Everything on it will be erased.
Ventoy, from the Tools screen or the ISO Library.
The ISO files you want, downloaded from the ISO Library pages.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Install Ventoy onto the stick with Ventoy2Disk. Check the drive letter and size twice before clicking Install.
Open the stick in File Explorer and copy the ISO files onto it. Folders are fine.
Safely eject the stick.
On the computer to repair, plug the stick in and switch on while tapping the boot menu key (often F12, F9, F8 or Esc; Dell uses F12, HP uses F9 or Esc, Lenovo uses F12).
Choose the USB stick, then pick an ISO from the Ventoy menu.

sections.heading: Which image for which job
steps: Windows will not start and you need files off it: Hiren's BootCD PE or a Linux live system.
Suspected memory fault, random crashes: Memtest86+, several passes.
Clone a drive to a new SSD: Rescuezilla or Clonezilla.
Resize or fix partitions: GParted Live.
Malware that blocks scanners inside Windows: ESET SysRescue Live.
Reinstall or repair-install Windows: the Windows 11 or 10 installer.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: If the stick does not appear in the boot menu, turn off Fast Startup in Windows or hold Shift while choosing Restart, and check that USB boot is allowed in the firmware settings.
A drive protected by BitLocker cannot be read from a rescue system without its recovery key. Get the key from the owner's Microsoft account first.

title: Rufus
summary: Writes an ISO to a USB stick to make it bootable.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Making a single-purpose bootable stick, most often a Windows installer.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Plug in the USB stick and open Rufus. Check the Device box shows the right stick.
Click SELECT and choose the ISO file.
Leave Partition scheme on GPT for computers made since about 2012, or MBR for older BIOS-only ones.
Click START. For a Windows 11 ISO, Rufus offers to remove the TPM, Secure Boot and online account requirements.
Wait for READY, then close and eject.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The status bar turns green and shows READY when the stick is finished.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: START erases the whole stick. Unplug other USB drives first.

title: Everything
summary: Finds any file by name instantly.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding a customer's lost documents, or every copy of a file, in seconds.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Everything and let it index the drives the first time (a few seconds).
Type part of the file name. Results narrow as you type.
Use "*.pdf" for a file type, or "folder: name" style filters from the Search menu.
Right-click a result for Open Path to jump to its folder.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Results list name, path, size and date. Click a column to sort; sorting by Date Modified shows recent work first.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: It searches names, not the text inside files.

title: WizTree
summary: Very fast map of what is using disk space.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding what filled a drive, in seconds rather than minutes.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run WizTree as administrator so it can read the drive index directly.
Choose the drive and click Scan.
The Tree View lists folders largest first. The File View lists the largest single files.
Right-click an item to open its folder or delete it.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The % of Parent column shows each folder's share. Work down from the biggest.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not delete inside Windows or Program Files from here.
Free for personal use; a business needs a supporter licence.

title: CPU-Z
summary: Identifies the processor, motherboard and memory exactly.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding the exact processor, motherboard model and memory type before ordering upgrades.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open CPU-Z and wait for it to read the hardware.
CPU tab: processor name, socket and core count.
Mainboard tab: motherboard maker, model and BIOS version.
Memory tab: total size, type (DDR3, DDR4, DDR5) and speed. SPD tab: each slot, with the module maker and part number.
Tools, then Save Report as HTML, keeps a record for the job.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: On the SPD tab, an empty slot shows blank fields. Match new memory to the type and speed shown there.

title: GPU-Z
summary: Identifies the graphics card and reads its sensors.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Confirming which graphics card is fitted, checking for counterfeit cards, and watching graphics temperature and load.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open GPU-Z. The Graphics Card tab shows the model, memory and driver version.
Use the drop-down at the bottom to switch between cards on a laptop with two.
The Sensors tab shows temperature, fan speed, load and memory use. Click a value to show its maximum.
Tick "Log to file" on the Sensors tab to record readings during a test.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: A card whose name shows a warning triangle may be a relabelled fake.
A graphics temperature above about 90 C under load needs attention.

title: CrystalDiskMark
summary: Measures how fast a drive reads and writes.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Checking whether a drive performs as it should, and showing the gain after an SSD upgrade.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Close other programs. Open CrystalDiskMark and choose the drive at the top right.
Click All. The test takes a few minutes.
Run it before and after an upgrade for a comparison.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The top row (SEQ1M) is large-file speed in MB/s: around 100 to 150 for a hard drive, 500 for a SATA SSD, 2000 and up for NVMe.
The bottom row (RND4K) is small-file speed, which is what makes a computer feel fast. Hard drives score about 1 MB/s here.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: The test writes to the drive. Avoid running it repeatedly on a nearly worn-out SSD.

title: OCCT
summary: Stress-tests the processor, memory, graphics and power supply.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Proving a repair after overheating, and finding faults that only appear under load.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open OCCT and choose a test on the left: CPU, Memory, 3D Standard (graphics) or Power.
Set a duration; 30 minutes is a reasonable bench test.
Click the start button and watch the temperature graphs.
OCCT stops by itself if it detects an error or a dangerous temperature.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Zero errors at the end of the run is a pass.
Errors in the CPU or Memory test point to faulty memory, an unstable processor or overheating.
A sudden shutdown or restart during the Power test points to the power supply.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Stress tests push hardware hard. Watch temperatures and stop if they pass the limits.
The free edition is for personal use.

title: Recuva
summary: Recovers deleted files from drives and memory cards.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Getting back files deleted by mistake, including after the Recycle Bin was emptied.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Install or run Recuva from a different drive than the one the files were on.
Follow the wizard: choose the file type and where the files were.
Run the normal scan first. Use Deep Scan only if the files are not found; it takes much longer.
Tick the files to recover and choose a folder on a different drive to save them to.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: A green dot means the file is intact, amber means partly overwritten, red means it is probably lost.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Stop using the drive as soon as files are lost. Every new file written lowers the chance of recovery.
Recovery from SSDs is often impossible because the drive erases deleted data by itself.

title: BlueScreenView
summary: Reads Windows crash dump files and names the driver involved.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding which driver or part is behind blue screens.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open BlueScreenView. It reads C:\Windows\Minidump automatically.
The top pane lists each crash with its date, error name and the driver blamed.
Click a crash. The bottom pane highlights the drivers on the stack at the time.
Options, then Advanced Options, opens dumps from another computer's drive.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The "Caused By Driver" column is the best single clue. The same driver across several crashes is the likely culprit.
ntoskrnl.exe is usually a bystander. When it is blamed every time with different error names, suspect memory.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: If the list is empty, Windows is not saving minidumps. Turn them on under System, Advanced system settings, Startup and Recovery.

title: Sysinternals TCPView
summary: Shows every program with a network connection open.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Seeing which programs are talking to the internet, and to where.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run TCPView as administrator.
Each row is one connection: the program, the local port, and the remote address and port.
Click the Remote Address column to group connections by destination.
Right-click a row for Close Connection or Kill Process, or Whois to look up who owns the address.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: New connections flash green and closed ones red.
A program you do not recognise holding a connection to an unfamiliar address is worth looking up before acting.

title: Sysinternals Process Monitor
summary: Records every file, registry and process event as it happens.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding out exactly why a program fails: which file it cannot open or which registry key it is missing.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run Process Monitor as administrator. It starts capturing immediately.
Press Ctrl+E to pause capture, and Ctrl+X to clear the list.
Set a filter (Ctrl+L): "Process Name is program.exe", then Add and OK.
Resume capture, reproduce the problem, then pause again.
Look in the Result column for ACCESS DENIED, NAME NOT FOUND and PATH NOT FOUND.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The Path column on a failing line names the file or key the program could not reach.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Captures grow very quickly. Capture for seconds, not minutes, and always filter.

title: Wireshark
summary: Captures and inspects network traffic.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Diagnosing network faults that simpler tests cannot explain: failed connections, slow name lookups, a device flooding the network.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Wireshark and double-click the network adapter that shows activity.
Reproduce the problem, then click the red square to stop.
Type a display filter in the bar: "dns", "tcp.port == 443", or "ip.addr == 192.168.1.50".
Statistics, then Conversations, shows which devices exchanged the most data.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Black rows with red text are errors such as retransmissions, a sign of a poor link.
A DNS query with no reply, or a long gap before it, explains slow page loads.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Only capture on networks you own or have permission to test. Captures can contain private data.

title: PuTTY
summary: Connects to other devices over SSH, Telnet or a serial cable.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Managing routers, switches, Linux computers and devices with a serial console.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open PuTTY. Type the address in Host Name and choose SSH (or Serial, with the COM port and speed).
Click Open and accept the host key the first time.
Log in with the device's user name and password.
Type a name under Saved Sessions and click Save to keep the settings.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: A login prompt means the connection works. "Connection refused" means SSH is off on the device; "timed out" means it cannot be reached.

title: Display Driver Uninstaller
summary: Completely removes graphics drivers so a clean one can be installed.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Fixing graphics crashes, black screens and failed driver updates by clearing out the old driver first.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Download the new graphics driver before you start.
Disconnect from the internet so Windows Update does not install a driver halfway through.
Restart into Safe Mode (hold Shift while clicking Restart, then Troubleshoot, Startup Settings).
Run DDU, choose GPU and the maker (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel), then "Clean and restart".
Back in normal Windows, install the new driver and reconnect.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: DDU shows a log as it works and restarts by itself when done. The screen will be low resolution until the new driver is in.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Let it create a restore point when it offers.

title: Snappy Driver Installer Origin
summary: Finds and installs missing or outdated drivers.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Getting network, chipset and other drivers onto a freshly installed computer, including one with no internet.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open SDIO. Choose "Download Indexes Only" the first time; it then lists the drivers this computer needs.
Tick the drivers to install. Start with chipset and network.
Tick "Create restore point", then click Install.
For offline use, download the full driver packs onto a USB drive on another computer.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Each driver shows a progress bar and a result. Restart when everything is finished.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Install only what is missing or faulty. Replacing working drivers can cause new problems.
Use the Origin edition from its own site; similarly named programs bundle unwanted software.

title: Revo Uninstaller
summary: Uninstalls programs and removes what they leave behind.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Removing stubborn programs, and cleaning up after an uninstaller that left files and registry entries.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Revo Uninstaller and select the program.
Click Uninstall. Revo makes a restore point and runs the program's own uninstaller.
Choose the Moderate scan when asked.
Review the leftover registry entries and files it lists, select them and click Delete.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Bold registry entries are the ones Revo will remove. Unbolded parents are shown only for context.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Use Moderate, not Advanced, unless you check every item yourself.

title: Angry IP Scanner
summary: Lists the devices on a network.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding the address of a printer, camera or other device on a network you look after.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Angry IP Scanner. The IP Range is filled in from your own network.
Click Start.
Blue dots are devices that answered. Columns show the name and response time.
Right-click a device to open it in a browser or copy its details.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Sort by the Hostname column to find a device by name. Tools, then Fetchers, adds columns such as the MAC maker.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Only scan networks you own or have permission to test.

title: TreeSize Free
summary: Shows folder sizes in a familiar Explorer-style tree.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding which folders are using the space, in a layout customers recognise.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run TreeSize Free as administrator to include every folder.
Choose the drive from Select Directory.
Expand the largest folders. Bars show each folder's share.
Right-click a folder to open it in Explorer.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Folders are sorted largest first. Switch the view between Size, Allocated and File Count on the ribbon.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Do not delete inside Windows or Program Files from here.

title: memtester
summary: Tests memory from inside a running Linux system.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: A quick memory check without restarting into a bootable tester.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Close other programs. Check free memory with "free -m".
Test most of the free memory for two passes: "sudo memtester 2048M 2" (2048M is the amount in megabytes).
Leave it to finish. Each pass runs a set of pattern tests.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Every test line should end in "ok". Any FAILURE means faulty memory.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: It can only test memory the system is not using. For a full test, boot Memtest86+ from the ISO Library.

title: stress-ng
summary: Loads the processor, memory and drives to prove stability.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Proving a repair after overheating, and reproducing faults that only appear under load.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: All processor cores for ten minutes: "stress-ng --cpu 0 --timeout 10m --metrics-brief".
Processor and memory together: "stress-ng --cpu 0 --vm 2 --vm-bytes 75% --timeout 10m".
Watch temperatures in another terminal with "watch -n 2 sensors".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "successful run completed" means no errors. Any "failed" count needs following up.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Stop with Ctrl+C if temperatures approach the critical value.

title: nvme-cli
summary: Reads health and wear data from NVMe SSDs.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Checking the wear and error counters of an NVMe SSD.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: List the drives: "sudo nvme list".
Health data: "sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0".
Error history: "sudo nvme error-log /dev/nvme0".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: percentage_used is the wear estimate; 100 means the rated life is used up.
available_spare below its threshold, or any media_errors, means back up and replace the drive.
critical_warning should be 0.

title: btop
summary: A clear, graphical-style view of processor, memory, disk and network use in the terminal.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Seeing at a glance what is loading the system.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run "btop".
Press f to filter processes by name, and use the arrow keys to select one.
Press Enter on a process for detail, k to end it, and m for the menu.
q quits.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The panels show processor load per core, memory and swap, disk activity and network speed, with the busiest processes listed underneath.

title: mtr
summary: Shows each hop between this computer and a destination, with loss and delay.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding where on the route a connection is slow or dropping.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Run "mtr 1.1.1.1" (macOS needs "sudo mtr").
Let it run for a minute, then press q.
For a report to send to a provider: "mtr -rwc 100 1.1.1.1".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Loss% that starts at one hop and continues to the last hop marks where the problem begins.
Loss at a single middle hop that does not continue is normal; that router just ignores test messages.
The first hop is your own router. Loss there is a local Wi-Fi or cable problem.

title: fwupd
summary: Updates firmware for the computer and its devices on Linux.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Installing BIOS, SSD and dock firmware updates on supported hardware.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: List what it can update: "fwupdmgr get-devices".
Refresh the catalogue: "fwupdmgr refresh".
See available updates: "fwupdmgr get-updates".
Install them: "fwupdmgr update". The computer may restart to finish.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "No updates available" means everything supported is current. Devices not listed are not supported by their maker.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Keep a laptop on mains power during a firmware update, and do not interrupt it.

title: rkhunter
summary: Checks a Linux system for rootkits and suspicious changes.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: A security check on a Linux system that may have been compromised.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Update its data: "sudo rkhunter --update".
Record the current state of system files on a known-clean system: "sudo rkhunter --propupd".
Run the check: "sudo rkhunter --check --sk".
Read the log at /var/log/rkhunter.log for the detail behind each warning.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Each test prints OK, Not found or Warning.
Warnings are common after ordinary package updates. Compare them with what was recently updated before worrying.

title: lshw
summary: Lists the hardware in a Linux computer in detail.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Getting model numbers for memory, drives and adapters before ordering parts.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Short overview: "sudo lshw -short".
One kind of hardware: "sudo lshw -C memory", "-C disk" or "-C network".
Save a full report: "sudo lshw -html > hardware.html".

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Under memory, each bank is a slot; "empty" marks a free one, with the size, type and speed of the fitted modules alongside.
"UNCLAIMED" beside a device means no driver is loaded for it.

title: Stats
summary: Shows processor, memory, temperature and network readings in the Mac menu bar.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Keeping an eye on temperatures and load on a Mac.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Stats. Icons appear in the menu bar.
Click an icon for its detail panel.
Open the settings from any panel to choose which modules show and which sensors appear.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The Sensors module lists temperatures and fan speeds. A processor near 100 C with fans at full speed points to dust or a failed fan.

title: OnyX
summary: Runs macOS maintenance tasks and rebuilds caches and indexes.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Clearing damaged caches and rebuilding system databases when a Mac misbehaves.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Use the OnyX version made for the installed macOS version.
Open OnyX and let it check the startup disk.
On the Maintenance tab, leave the default ticks and click Run Tasks.
The Mac restarts when the tasks finish.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The first start afterwards is slower while caches rebuild. That is expected.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Leave the options at their defaults unless you know what each one does.

title: coconutBattery
summary: Shows a Mac battery's health, cycle count and age.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Deciding whether a MacBook battery needs replacing.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open coconutBattery.
Read "Design capacity" against "Full charge capacity", and the cycle count.
Plug in an iPhone or iPad to read its battery from the iOS Device tab.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Full charge capacity under about 80% of design, or a cycle count past the model's limit (usually 1000), means the battery is due for replacement.

title: GrandPerspective
summary: Maps what is using disk space on a Mac.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Finding what filled a Mac's drive.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open GrandPerspective and choose the drive or folder to scan.
Each rectangle is a file; its area is its size. Hover to see the path.
Select a block and click Reveal to open it in Finder.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The largest rectangles are the largest files. Common finds are old iPhone backups, video files and virtual machines.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Give it Full Disk Access in System Settings, Privacy and Security, or it cannot see everything.

title: AppCleaner
summary: Removes a Mac app together with its support files.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Fully removing an app, where dragging it to the Trash leaves files behind.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open AppCleaner.
Drag the app from Applications onto the window, or pick it from the list.
Review the files it found and click Remove.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: The list shows the app and each related file with its size. Untick anything you want to keep.

title: Dell Command Update
summary: Dell's own tool for BIOS, firmware and driver updates.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Bringing a Dell computer's BIOS, firmware and drivers up to date from Dell directly.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open Dell Command Update and click CHECK.
Review the list. Updates are grouped as critical, recommended and optional.
Click INSTALL. Keep a laptop on mains power.
Restart when asked. A BIOS update finishes during the restart.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "This system is up to date" means nothing is outstanding.
The Update History view lists what was installed and when.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Never switch off during a BIOS update.
If BitLocker is on, suspend it before a BIOS update or have the recovery key ready.

title: Lenovo System Update
summary: Lenovo's own tool for BIOS, firmware and driver updates.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Bringing a Lenovo ThinkPad, ThinkCentre or IdeaPad up to date from Lenovo directly.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Open System Update and click Next to search.
Updates are listed as Critical, Recommended and Optional. Tick what to install.
Click Download, then let it install.
Restart when asked.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: An empty list means the computer is up to date.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Keep a laptop on mains power, and do not interrupt a BIOS update.
If BitLocker is on, suspend it before a BIOS update or have the recovery key ready.

title: Intel Driver and Support Assistant
summary: Finds and installs current drivers for Intel graphics, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and chipsets.

sections.heading: What it is for
steps: Updating Intel graphics, wireless and chipset drivers on any make of computer.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Start Intel Driver and Support Assistant from the Start menu. It opens a page in your browser.
Wait for the scan, then review the available updates.
Click Download beside each, then Install.
Restart when it has finished.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "Your system is up-to-date" means no Intel updates are outstanding.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Laptop makers sometimes customise graphics drivers. If the Intel driver refuses to install, use the maker's own update tool.
